meanings.note: For liking things, places or activities.
For loving a person; adding bien often softens the sense to liking them.

Imperative used to encourage.

examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: Une autre = another (one).

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.

examples.text: Tu as complètement perdu la tête!

ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel
at the end of a sentence: super, non?

meanings.note: Can express contempt, pathetic, or evoke pity, pitiful; context and tone distinguish them.

examples.text: Tu peux être tellement snob, Andréa. C'est pitoyable!
examples.trans: You can be such a snob, Andréa. It's pathetic!

meanings.note: With ne in a negative, no longer or no more.
In comparisons, more; plus tard means later and is pronounced without a final s sound.

examples.trans: I can't take any more, Andréa.

meanings.note: Liked or known by a broad public.
In other contexts, of ordinary people or working-class.

examples.text: Line Renaud est belle, du bon âge, et très populaire.

meanings.note: before an infinitive: pour faire plaisir
+ infinitive: pour voir.

examples.text: Je suis là pour voir Mathias.

meanings.note: A question word, also used in an indirect question after a verb such as comprendre.

examples.text: Pourquoi est-ce que tu ne m'as rien dit hier?
examples.trans: Why didn't you tell me anything yesterday?

examples.text: Je comprends enfin pourquoi elle a refusé ce film.
examples.trans: I finally understand why she turned down that film.

meanings.note: + infinitive.
conditional: tu pourrais, vous pourriez
Joins two parts: dis-lui que.
Relative: tout ce que.
With ne: ne... que.

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun.
Quelle surprise!.

examples.trans: How old would you say she is?

meanings.note: In qu’est-ce qui, the question expression supplies the subject, and need not refer to a person.
Interrogative what, especially in informal questions and after a preposition.

examples.text: Quoi, tu n'as pas encore lu le nouveau scénario?
examples.trans: What, you haven't read the new script yet?

examples.text: De quoi est-ce que vous parlez tous les deux?
examples.trans: What are the two of you talking about?

meanings.note: Put someone or something in another's place.
Can refer to a temporary stand-in as well as a permanent replacement.

examples.trans: We don't have to replace Françoise Fabian.

meanings.en: to humiliate oneself, to lose face

examples.trans: I'm not going to humiliate myself.

examples.trans: He doesn't want to lose face in front of her.

examples.text: Je ne vais pas m'humilier. Je sais qu'il dira non.
examples.trans: I'm not going to humiliate myself. I know he'll say no.

meanings.note: Rescue or save; can apply figuratively to a film, deal or project.

examples.text: J'ai sauvé une cliente de l'agence, c'est tout.

savoir.gloss: to know; to know how to

+ infinitive: savoir monter.
